title: Add Android/iOS branch coverage for NotificationGateway.requestPermission()/hasPermission()

evidence.quote: 'returns true when no platform-specific impl is available (non-mobile)',

why: resolvePlatformSpecificImplementation<AndroidFlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin>() (and the iOS equivalent) always return null against the mock plugin in a plain unit test, so requestPermission/hasPermission's tests only exercise the trivial fallback branch. The actual Android (POST_NOTIFICATIONS + exact-alarm) and iOS (alert/badge/sound) request logic -- the code that determines whether real users on real devices actually get permission requested correctly -- has no unit-test seam at all.
recommendation: Introduce a thin platform-request abstraction NotificationGateway can take a fake for, or verify mocktail can stub AndroidFlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin/IOSFlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin directly so the branch logic becomes testable.
acceptance_criteria: A test exercising the Android branch asserts both requestNotificationsPermission() and requestExactAlarmsPermission() are called and the granted flag is threaded through correctly; an equivalent test exists for iOS.

corrections: notification_gateway.dart quote "final android = _plugin..." begins at line 122, not 121 (line 121 is the method signature).
